hotspots.title: Summer 2004
hotspots.body: The third film opened in Britain at the end of May 2004 and in America a few days later: the first in the series to arrive in summer rather than before Christmas.

hotspots.title: A new eye
hotspots.body: Alfonso Cuarón took over as director and changed the texture of the series: handheld moments, students in their own clothes, and a darker, weather-beaten castle.

hotspots.title: A new tower
hotspots.body: The giant clock tower and its courtyard were added to the castle for this film, with a pendulum swinging through the passage below. Time becomes a theme you can see.

hotspots.title: Homework for the cast
hotspots.body: Cuarón reportedly asked his three young leads to write essays about their characters, and used what they wrote to talk about who those characters were becoming.

hotspots.title: A new headmaster
hotspots.body: Michael Gambon took over the role of the headmaster after Richard Harris's death, playing him for the rest of the series with a lighter, more restless energy.

hotspots.title: Highland weather
hotspots.body: Much of the outdoor feel came from the Scottish Highlands: Glencoe and its surroundings provided the brooding hills that frame the castle grounds in this film and later ones.

hotspots.title: A hut on the hill
hotspots.body: The gamekeeper's hut was moved to a slope below the castle for this film, so that hill, hut and pumpkin patch sit against the sky. It is where an execution is awaited and a rescue begins.

hotspots.title: Half eagle, half horse
hotspots.body: The proud hippogriff was mostly digital, but life-size models were built for the cast to stroke and bow to, and the animators studied real birds for the way the creature carried itself.

hotspots.title: Williams' last
hotspots.body: This was John Williams' final score for the series, written with a medieval flavour and recorders. It was nominated for an Academy Award, as were the visual effects.

hotspots.title: Cold that you can see
hotspots.body: The prison guards drain warmth from the air: windows frost over, water ices, breath turns white. The film makes their arrival a weather event before it is a monster.

hotspots.title: The shortest book-length film so far
hotspots.body: At about 142 minutes it was the shortest film in the series up to that point, compressing a dense book into a quick, playful puzzle.

collectibles.name: A feather
collectibles.note: Too large for any bird you know.
